messages:
sam: Hey team, seeing p95 east-west latency spikes during the 200-260s batching window on cluster-gpu-us-east. Normally ~0.8ms, jumping to 12-30ms for ~40s and coincides with increased retransmits and TX drops on a subset of hosts. Anyone else seeing this?
anya: Yep, I caught alerts. Affected nodes: gpu-az1-12/13/14, gpu-az1-21. Packet loss on bond0 increasing during the window (ifconfig shows RX errors rising).
ricardo: Can you paste the tcpdump or iftop? Also check ethtool -S and dmesg for mlx errors.
sam: Pasting quick snippets: 
```
$ ifconfig bond0
bond0: flags=4163<UP,BROADCAST,RUNNING,MULTICAST> mtu 9000
  RX packets 1253456 errors:0 dropped:0 overruns:0 frame:0

$ ifconfig bond0 (on gpu-az1-21)
bond0: flags=4163<UP,BROADCAST,RUNNING,MULTICAST> mtu 1500
  RX packets 1253750 errors:0 dropped:1203 overruns:0 frame:0
```
ricardo: Interesting — mtu mismatch between peers (9000 vs 1500) will fragment or cause host CPU fallback for RoCE. What does ethtool -k show?
anya: On gpu-az1-12: `ethtool -k ens224` shows GRO/TSO/SG on. On gpu-az1-21 TSO/GRO are off after last config push.
eng-infra-oncall: Noted. Any recent CM/ansible runs or netconfig pushes? I see a small netcfg change deployed ~14:03 by infra-config job.
icola: I pulled the deploy log: deploy-bot triggered netcfg/mtu-change for az1 group at 14:02 to standardize to 1500 (theres a ticket about interop), but it skipped marking RDMA hosts. Looks like the playbook applied to some GPU hosts accidentally.
deploy-bot: automated deploy: netcfg/mtu-change v2 -> applied to targets: gpu-az1-21,gpu-az1-22,gpu-az1-23 at 14:02:11. (owner: infra-config)
sam: That matches timing with the spike. For RoCE/ib devices, MTU mismatch causes fragmentation and driver fallback increasing latency during heavy KV cache fetches while batching.
ricardo: Steps: 1) drain gpu-az1-21/22/23 from scheduling for batch windows, 2) revert MTU 1500->9000 on those hosts, 3) verify RDMA link using `ibv_devinfo` and `rdma link` and run short pings.
anya: On it — draining pods now (cordon+drain).
eng-infra-oncall: I'll open a rollback for the netcfg change and mark infra-config on notice.
nicola: After revert, run a 2-min load test mimicking batching to confirm p95 stable.
ricardo: Also check for backlog in NAPI/interrupts during the spike: `cat /proc/interrupts` and `sar -n DEV 1 30` to see interface drops.
sam: Rolling revert on gpu-az1-21 now: `ansible-playbook netcfg_revert.yml -i hosts/gpu-az1-21 -e mtu=9000`
sam: Revert finished, ethtool shows MTU 9000 and TSO/GRO back on. RX drops reset to 0.
anya: Running 3-minute synthetic batch load against the pair. Initial p95: 0.9ms. Load at 200-260s window: p95 remained ~1.1ms, no spike.
eng-infra-oncall: Good. I've filed incident INC-2026-114 and assigned to infra-config for root cause (playbook scoping bug).
nicola: Action items: add explicit host tag exclusion for rdma/roce hosts in netcfg playbook, add a preflight check to compare MTU across RDMA peers before applying, and add a canary that targets a single non-production host first.
ricardo: Also consider alerting on sudden MTU drift for a rack (monitor config drift via config management telemetry).
sam: Thanks all. Moving affected machines back into rotation. Will watch for recurrence during next peak window.
eng-infra-oncall: Closing on-call loop. If you see anything sticky, mention @eng-infra-oncall. :thumbsup:
